decisions.question: Run 2 of the Salesforce chess case stopped at the cap with ShipLoop active at `test` of work item 2 of 2. What is the next live round and its budget: resume run 2, a fresh run on released 2.5.0, go straight to the plan-implemented run, or change the case first?

options.label: A. Resume run 2 once, to done, on its original 1.4.0 build, in the background, no keep
options.effect: Finishes the SDLC on a hosted platform for the first time: runs the 9 outer stages never run live (the plan's per-packet rows 16 to 24 are estimates) and the rest of item 2; may be the case's first pass; gives the time-to-done control. The harness already supports it (the case's resume_note tells the model the org was reset and to deploy again).
options.cost: Projected 1.7 h (range 1.1 to 2.8) and about $10 (range $7 to 17). Basis: Grok segment 2 measured $12.21 for 7,202 s and 428 turns = $6.10/h; remaining = item 2 test/document/verify/carry-forward 0.3 to 0.55 h plus 9 outer stages at the measured mean of 538 s per stage. Needs --timeout 10800 (7200 hit the cap) and --max-budget-usd 20.
options.risk: Old build: measures nothing about 2.5.0 or the plan. Cannot keep the app (the run folder is under $TMPDIR; README requires a durable --output for --keep-platform). Org busy until the cleanup. Grok login and quota unchecked. The folder can be purged after days.

options.label: B. Fresh run on released 2.5.0 first
options.effect: Measures the credential removal (live2 had zero refused submissions, so there is nothing to see) and not the Skill-call hook (Claude-only, D-24).
options.cost: Projected 5 to 6 h and $30 to 37 (4.04 h already spent plus the 1.7 h remaining, at $6.10/h).
options.risk: Near-duplicate of the final run; a third stop at a 4 h cap is likely; the default contract deletes a working app on a timeout (keep_refusal: 'the host timed out').

options.label: C. Go straight to the plan-implemented run (fresh, --source checkout, --keep-platform, durable --output)
options.effect: Lowest spend and the run the owner asked for on 2026-10-17. The outer stages are first met at hour 4 or later.
options.cost: Projected 4.3 to 4.9 h (old-build 5.7 h less 15 to 25% from the plan's levers) and $26 to 30; a 6 h cap = $37.
options.risk: An outer-stage platform problem (permission classifier, guard, release or operations stage on an org) is found late; today's contract cleans the working app on a timeout.

options.label: D. Change the case first (smaller scope, cheaper model)
options.effect: A shorter, cheaper run.
options.cost: Not measured. Gives up the owner's 'playable chess app that remains'; Grok 4.7 medium is the owner's execution default.
options.risk: Moves the target after one miss; evidence not comparable with run 2.

decisions.recommendation: Order: (1) now, no go needed (proactively-run-verification): one Claude Sonnet 5.5 node-fix-bug slice on main da9e2e75 (= 2.5.0), `python3 test/shiploop_e2e/slice.py --case node-fix-bug --host claude`, to measure the Skill-call hook (improve skill invoked in 4 of 4 Improve stages, was 1 of 4 on 1.3.0) and the credential removal; cost is unreported by the slice harness, projected $1 to 2 (70 turns x $0.0187). (2) With your go, option A in the background while the plan is implemented: --timeout 10800, --max-budget-usd 20, one resume, stop only on a fatal block, no keep. (3) Before the final run land a harness-only keep-on-cap rule: also keep when the org checks (deployed, tests, rules) pass, the trial is valid and the host timed out, recorded 'not a pass'; never after a user stop or an invalid trial; README text and a test with it. (4) Final run = option C: fresh, --source checkout, --keep-platform with a durable --output, two 10,800 s segments (6 h), --max-budget-usd 45. Projected total $40 to 55.
decisions.rationale: The hook only exists on Claude, so only a Claude slice can measure it; the credential removal cannot show in this case (0 refusals); the cap, not the app, ended run 2 (deployed, tests and rules passed 28 of 28 at the stop), so the cap and the keep rule are the two cheap levers; the resume runs in the background while the plan is built, so it costs no session time and finds the unmeasured outer-stage problems at about $10 instead of at hour 4 of a $30 run. Changing the case gives up the owner's goal. Consistent with batch-run-to-completion (resume stopped runs in place), proactively-run-verification, experiments-use-sonnet (Grok 4.7 medium execution) and the one-at-a-time-against-the-org rule.

decisions.question: What should the verification battery be after the next release: which cases, hosts and models, how many paired runs, which clears of context, and how is it decided by a script?

options.label: A. The plan's full design at every release: 5 arms x 2 cases x 2 hosts, six clears per slice (about 20 slices)
options.effect: Strongest evidence for the start-here card and entry-card workstream.
options.cost: Projected $100 to 140 and 12 h or more of Grok wall time (20 slices x about 250 turns x $0.0187 Claude or $0.0285 Grok per turn).
options.risk: Contradicts 'one live verification run per release' and testing-scope-to-change; clears inside one slice are not independent samples; most arms exist only to choose the card design, which is a one-time decision.

options.label: B. Hard gates plus exact bytes, 6 slices per release that changes what the model reads
options.effect: Decides S-6 by zero redone calls, and bytes by an offline render (exact), with time and tokens descriptive. Slices: node-fix-bug inline on Claude Sonnet 5.5 (control, candidate) and on Grok 4.7 medium (control, candidate); node-add-function as a two-step ask-agent chain on Claude (control, candidate). Six clears per slice: step-plan, implement, test, verify, carry-forward and one Improve window; Claude at boundary and inside, Grok at boundaries only (clear.py gates :inside only on Claude streams); resume prompt withheld.
options.cost: Projected about $33 and 2.5 h wall (4 Claude + 2 Grok slices; Claude 3.2 s and $0.0187 per turn, Grok 16.8 s and $0.0285 per turn, about 250 turns per slice). Slice cost is unreported by the harness, so these are projections.
options.risk: Detects frequent failure only: 0 failures in the 18 candidate clears bounds the per-clear failure rate below 17% (rule of three, 95%).

options.label: C. Offline renders plus two small full runs
options.effect: Cheap (hello costs $3.69 on average); proves bytes and head budgets only.
options.cost: About $8 projected.
options.risk: No clear-the-context evidence, which the main tenet (S-6) requires before any consolidation.

options.label: D. Compare time, turns and cost between arms at n=2 to 3
options.effect: Looks like a quick answer.
options.cost: Cheap per run.
options.risk: Measured spread of nine identical Claude hello runs: turns CV 0.32, cost CV 0.38, planning seconds CV 0.33. A 10% effect needs about 160 runs per arm and a 25% effect about 26 (n = 2 x (2.8 x CV / effect)^2). It cannot decide.

decisions.recommendation: Option B, decided by arms.py (plan 1.3; it does not exist yet). Every release: Tier 0 with no model (G-SUITES, G-LEDGER, G-RENDER, head table). Only a release that changes packet text or order, the entry card, the loop block, Improve text or a hook adds Tier 1 = the 6 slices above, control = the previous release's pinned sha re-run the same day (host builds drift), A/A spread = 2 control runs per host and case, taken once and again when the host build changes, kept in the journal. arms.py decides in this order: hard gates (zero redone state-changing calls in every clear; first-pass refusals per verb not above control plus the A/A spread; warm `next` calls not above control; no lost ledger obligation; no flipped SPEC clause; on Claude the improve skill invoked in every Improve stage), then exact bytes ingested, then time and tokens descriptive only; it exits non-zero without a decision or when the difference is inside the A/A spread. Judge only where text moves: Opus 5.5 medium, one per round, blind to arm, for the seeded-defect catch and the retention rubric. Codex: one smoke slice (Luna xhigh) on the efficiency release only, not a gate. Prerequisite: make SEED_SCRIPT capture the item base, otherwise every slice skips the base run, mutation gate, change inventory and item commit. The Salesforce run (P1) and hello/checkers n=2 full runs belong to the plan release, not to every release.
decisions.rationale: Follows eval-decision-priority (material quality first, then tokens, then time; thresholds are the control's own spread, never invented), testing-scope-to-change, proactively-run-verification and the plan's own principle 10. S-6 is a hard property, so zero redone calls is the right gate, not a mean. Time, turns and cost cannot decide at any affordable n (measured CV 0.32 to 0.38); bytes are exact offline; refusals, warm next calls and redone calls are counts that move by large factors when a pointer works.

options.label: A. Push the docs commit to main now (after adding run 2's baseline row), and back up the three feature branches as non-main branches

options.cost: Minutes. `bash test/run-all.sh --group quick --changed-from origin/main` first; docs-only, so CI is not watched.

options.label: B. Hold everything for the next release

options.cost: None now.

options.risk: More handling for little gain; a dated plan revision marked superseded is the normal practice in this repo (journal: 'edit later rather than deleting').

decisions.recommendation: Option A, with your go. Also committed but unpublished: nothing else on a branch. Uncommitted: that baseline row; `p_step.txt` (71 KB untracked packet dump in the main checkout, safe to delete). Not in any repo: the scratchpad studies and this study's output, and run 2's compact review-export.json (41 KB, last written before the final state).

decisions.question: Which follow-ups from the credential-removal review (CR-1, CR-4, CR-5, CR-6), the guard `.gitkeep` false block and the Apex-output reading by ShipLoop's red-check and mutation steps (D-25, a platform-declared test adapter) go now, later or never?

options.label: A. Everything now, including the D-25 adapter
options.effect: Closes every open row.
options.cost: The adapter is a new mechanism (platform-declared reporter vocabulary plus 'run against the base') on top of the 36-unit plan.
options.risk: Delays the final live run; violates KISS-over-adversarial-guards for CR-4, CR-5 and CR-6, which break nothing.

options.label: B. Triage by 'did a real run hit it and does it mislead the normal path' (recommended)
options.effect: Fixes the three things the Salesforce case hit or depends on and documents the rest.
options.cost: One small commit: one test, one guard line with its test, one platform-card paragraph and one pointer sentence.
options.risk: The card text may not be enough for the Apex reporter (unverified); then the adapter code follows, with evidence.

options.label: C. Document all, fix none
options.effect: No work.
options.cost: None.
options.risk: Leaves two defects observed in the very case that must pass: the false block and the unreadable Apex reporter.

decisions.recommendation: Option B. NOW (before the final live run): (1) CR-1: one acceptance test through the real gate, a reviewed stage whose summary holds `Auth: sf login (alias de)` starts its Improve child (the Salesforce case writes such text: 4 of 29 accepted live2 results mention sf login, credential or access token). (2) The `.gitkeep` false block: in test/shiploop_e2e/checks/sf_guard.py a default-scope deploy of an empty directory is refused as 'not a class, tab, app or app page named SLChess*' (1 of the 2 denials in 140 calls); skip the exact name `.gitkeep` in the scope walk, plus one test in shiploop-e2e-sf-guard. (3) The Apex reporter, text only (the first half of D-25): in references/platforms/salesforce.md state which reporter flag ShipLoop can read and that an org-bound test cannot fail on the base unless the command deploys the tree (so red_na with its reason is the route); make the 'unread' refusal in shiploop_test_loop._explain_base name the platform card instead of listing only node, pytest, unittest and jest. LATER: CR-4 (fold the retired-phrase list of shiploop-packet-completeness over `shiploop reference` text and SKILL.md the next time that test is edited; no stale text exists today); the adapter code only if the final run still hits 'unread' with the card in place. NEVER: CR-5 (the journal already records that the commit message's byte savings do not reproduce: 32 per inner stage, 65 step-plan, 289 over 12 packets, not 345; do not rewrite the commit), CR-6 (fix the one test comment when that file is next touched; the dated 2026-10-11 doc is history), CR-2/CR-3 (display-only, known: the display screen flags 0 of 29 live2 results).
decisions.rationale: KISS over adversarial guards and 'question the value of every change': fix only what breaks or misleads a normal run. CR-1 protects the path the removal changed and the Salesforce case exercises; the false block and the unreadable reporter were observed in run 2 (the test stage of item 1 took 361 s blocked, 1,163 s revise and 428 s; the 'unread' sentence appears 21 times in the event stream, not de-duplicated). The adapter is a separate plan (D-25) and a text card is the cheapest test of whether code is needed.

decisions.question: How should the inner-loop redesign artifact become the owner's iteration tool: what to add or change, how is it refreshed, and what is its consumer contract?

options.label: A. Keep hand-publishing the static page and fix the findings by editing the HTML
options.effect: Fastest first fix of the wrong figures.
options.cost: Each refresh rewrites a 608 KB page; effort not measured.
options.risk: The builder (build_page.py, run_page.py) exists nowhere I could find (searched the scratchpad and ~/src), so every refresh is manual and the unit errors below recur.

options.label: B. Rebuild the page from run files with a script in the repo, on top of flow.py, with a script-derived Read-first panel
options.effect: Every figure comes from files (events.jsonl, metrics.json, packet archive); the step cards reuse flow.json; one implementation of the mechanism.
options.cost: A repo script plus a test; effort not measured. The panel itself is small: the cross reviewer recomputed every panel fact with about 6 KB of throwaway scripts.
options.risk: The page changes shape; the status/decision content (status.json: change log, 5 decisions, 14 open items) needs a committed home.

options.label: C. Option B plus the db capability for decisions (tick accept, reject or defer; a session reads it with ArtifactData; a copy-prompt button as fallback)
options.effect: The owner can answer D-n and P-n items on the page and the next session reads the answers; the same pattern as the Run Review and Technique Atlas pages.
options.cost: One collection (decisions) and a small panel; the artifact currently declares no capabilities, so a republish with `capabilities` is needed.
options.risk: One more mutable surface; keep it to id, status, owner note and updatedAt.

options.label: D. Fold everything into the Run Review page

decisions.recommendation: Option C, built as B first. WHAT TO CHANGE, from the cross-cutting findings (X-10, X-11, X-12) and the page text I read: (1) A script-derived 'Read first' panel above the method text, each figure linked to its file: ShipLoop commands run, how many literal, how many cut by `| head` (median N), status displays fired (the recorded run: all 20 `complete` calls piped, display fired 1 of 21 commands); per producer stage chars written versus chars the model saw and whether the packet file was opened (3 of 8); per step seconds, turns and context tokens (60,063 to 152,716); gates that ran versus skipped (4 skipped); refusals by stage and cause (3, all test-spec check-only); item commit present (no); skills invoked (improve 1 of 4). (2) Fix the compare table: both columns on-disk chars from `packets.py --compare`, handoff rows added, seed packet excluded, percent shown (the page shows step-plan 22,292 against the 28,303 its own step header gives; producers are -10.4% on one basis, not -29.8%; handoffs 155,141 to 156,284, +0.7%); label time and turns n=1 (the same case spans 162 to 269 s across builds). (3) A staleness banner: 'recorded <date> on <sha>, main <sha>, N packet-generator commits since' (the page says 1.3.0 while its dashboard describes 2.5.0). (4) Decisions with ids (D-n, P-n) and a status, kept in the db. (5) Say what the run cannot show: 'warm inline context; recovery after a clear not measured', and annotate the failed Skill call and the unknown-skill detour on step-plan. (6) Small fixes: rename 'What reached the model' to 'Seen by the model (after any | head)', show each Improve packet under the step whose response printed it, tag host-injected skill text, collapse contract and receipt JSON (79,700 chars, 13%), expand-all, per-event anchors, pin mermaid to an exact version (it loads mermaid@11). HOW REFRESHED: the builder is committed (a mode of test/shiploop_e2e/flow.py plus a page wrapper, not a new tool; status content committed under docs/), rebuilt after every run and every merged change group in the same turn (owner rule), PDT stamp and shas set at build time, same URL. Also publish run 2 and the 2.5.0 slice through the existing shiploop-run-review skill rather than by hand. CONSUMER CONTRACT: the owner, in a browser, after each run or change group and at the start of a session; first screen = Read-first panel + open decisions with ids; below that the step cards; every figure links to its file; a time or turn delta is never shown without n and the A/A spread; a Claude Code session reads it with `Artifact read` and the decisions with ArtifactData. The page's next content is the 2.5.0 slice from P1 step 1, with the recorded 1.3.0 run as the 'before'.
